name: Overhead transmission lines (132-500 kV)
applications: bulk grid transmission in Peninsular Malaysia
principle: The transmission backbone: TNB operates 132 kV, 275 kV and 500 kV lines. Insulator creepage and clearance are set by the phase voltage and local pollution; the tower type (lattice steel or monopole) follows terrain and corridor constraints; ACSR or AAAC conductors are sized by ampacity and sag; earth wires or line surge arresters protect against lightning, which matters heavily in Malaysia's thunderstorm climate. Live-line working and patrols carry the lifecycle.

suppliers.name: Tenaga Nasional Berhad (TNB)
suppliers.product: owner and operator of the Peninsular grid

performance.metric: transmission voltage levels in Peninsular Malaysia
performance.basis: TNB transmission at 132 kV, 275 kV and 500 kV
TNB 500 kV short-circuit rating 50 kA for 1 s
TNB 132 kV 31.5 kA for 3 s, 40 kA near power stations

sources.note: TNB transmission, voltage and fault-level tables, read 2026-11-13

costs.metric: total installed cost, new single-circuit overhead line
costs.basis: MISO 2023 USD, $/mile converted: 230 kV $2.1-2.5M/mile (~$1.3-1.6M/km), 345 kV $3.4-3.9M/mile (~$2.1-2.4M/km), 500 kV $4.2-4.8M/mile (~$2.6-3.0M/km). Total installed, excludes land. Terrain is priced as adders, not in the base: forested clearing $5,995/acre, mountainous $794/acre, wetland $69,975/acre plus $56,132/acre mitigation. A terrain-priced cross-check from Western Power (330 kV, A$1.17M/km rural to A$2.24M/km urban) sits in the same order.

source.note: MISO Transmission Cost Estimation Guide for MTEP24 (Jan 2024), 2023 USD: line, transformer and site-work tables, read 2026-11-16
